content.title: What is the goal of NASA's Artemis II program and moon mission?
content.text: The NASA Artemis program is taking a major step forward with its first crewed mission around the moon in more than five decades. The mission will send four astronauts aboard the Orion spacecraft to test systems and lay the groundwork for future exploration.NASA official Dr. Joe Westlake spoke about the mission’s goals, what astronauts will experience and how it fits into long-term plans for a sustained human presence beyond Earth. Key Takeaways NASA’s Artemis mission marks the first crewed trip around the moon in more than 50 years, testing the Orion spacecraft.The program aims to establish a long-term lunar base to support research and future missions to Mars.Astronauts will travel hundreds of thousands of miles, seeing the far side of the moon and unique views of Earth in space. What is the Artemis mission trying to accomplish? Westlake said the mission is a critical first step in returning humans to the moon and preparing for deeper space exploration.“You know, as these astronauts set out for the first time in 50 years towards the moon, to be able to actually travel and wring out the understanding of the Orion capsule and the Artemis program, you know, these are our first steps with this manned crewed test mission out towards the moon and out towards setting a permanent human presence out at the moon with our lunar base.” Why is this mission important right now? Westlake said the Artemis program is designed to go beyond short visits to the moon and build toward long-term exploration goals.“Yeah, I mean, we’re looking for the opportunity to be able to put that lunar base out there, to be able to do new research, to be able to test and wring out our technologies and eventually get ourselves to a position where we can put human feet on Mars.” What will astronauts experience on the journey? The mission will take astronauts hundreds of thousands of miles from Earth, offering views few humans have ever seen.Westlake said they will watch Earth fade into the distance as the moon grows larger and may even witness a solar eclipse during the trip. He also said the crew will see parts of the moon never visible from Earth.“As these astronauts go across the far side of the moon, they’re going to see a totally different face than what we see here on Earth.” Space health scientists from around the globe are in Tulsa this week for an event held on the OSU Tulsa campus. One of the speakers is NASA astronaut Victor Glover, who is scheduled to pilot the Artemis II. Glover joins us on Six In The Morning to share more. January 24, 2024 08:28 AM2 min read How have astronauts prepared for this mission? Westlake said the crew has spent years training to ensure a safe and successful mission.“They’ve been preparing for this mission for years. And they’ve been moving towards ensuring the safe flight, ensuring that they’re able to bring back science and understanding and their own perspective as we go out to the moon.”He added the astronauts represent “the best of what humanity brings forward” and will provide a human perspective on deep space travel. What are the long-term goals beyond this mission? According to Westlake, Artemis is part of a broader effort to expand human presence in space.The program aims to establish a lunar base that can support ongoing research and serve as a launching point for future missions to Mars.Westlake said the mission is meant to inspire a new generation and represents a shared effort.“This mission is for all Americans, it is for humanity. It is for our trek out into the stars.” What factors could impact the launch? Weather remains a key factor in any space launch.Westlake said conditions appear favorable, noting sunny skies and manageable winds in Florida, though teams continue to monitor conditions closely.“Everything looks pretty good… for right now, that launch condition… looks pretty good as we go out into the future.” Copy Link copied Email Print Brooke Cox is a Digital Producer at News On 6, where she has been part of the team since August 2024.
